newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia state oil company sets goals for '97.
newsitem.headline: Colombia state oil company sets goals for '97.

text.p: The value of Colombia's oil exports is expected to show a year-on-year rise of almost 25 percent by the end of 1996 and is forecast to grow another 17 percent by the end of 1997, a report by state oil company Ecopetrol said Monday.

In the year to November the value of Colombia's total oil exports reached a historic high of $1.43 billion and that figure is on track to surpass $1.5 billion by the end of this year, Ecopetrol said in its report entitled "Results 1996, Aims 1997".
It forecast the value of exports to hit $1.76 billion by the end of 1997, fueled by the boom in production expected in the Cusiana and Cupiagua fields.

British Petroleum Ltd Plc, the main operator in those two fields, and Colombia's largest single foreign investor, says output will hit 500,000 barrels per day by the end of 1997 -- up from current levels of 175,000 barrels per day.

Ecopetrol said its objectives for 1997 included boosting the country's oil production to 723,000 barrels per day from current levels of 638,000 barrels per day, improving the state-run oil refineries and pressing ahead with plans for the mass distribution of natural gas.

As part of its strategy to increase national oil output, Ecopetrol signed 19 new contracts with private firms in the course of this year, taking the number of the state-oil companies private sector associates to 65, about a third of which are foreign enterprises. Another five association contracts are being processed.

Ecopetrol said as many as 30 new test drills would be sunk in 1997, most of those by its private sector associates. It said it would drill up to six development wells and expected its associates to sink more than 60 new wells.
An additional 560 miles (900 km) of gas piepline is scheduled to be built during next year taking the total national network to 1,620 miles (2,600 km).

Ecopetrol has set a budget for 1997 of 175 billion pesos to modernize refining at its plants in the oil production center of Barrancabermeja, in central Colombia, and in Cartagena, on the Caribbean coast.

Throughput will remain at about current levels of 281,000 barrels a day but the state-run oil company hopes to improve safety and reduce wastage. refining processes more environmentally-friendly. Ecopetrol has earmarked an additional 27.9 billion pesos solely for making refining processes more environmentally-friendly.
